formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Anyone who submits the signature to permit() sets the OP allowance of owner for spender to exactly value. This replaces any earlier allowance and does not add to it.
The signature works only until deadline (block.timestamp <= deadline). It uses the owner's current nonce, and each use raises that nonce by one.
The spender can then move up to value OP from the owner with transferFrom. Only an allowance of type(uint256).max is never used up.
formats.shown: The intent "Authorize spending of tokens", then the spender address in raw form, the cap in OP ("250 OP", or "Unlimited" at or above 2^255), the deadline as a date, and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit test only covers a finite amount; the "Unlimited" threshold message is never exercised.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json message.value "250000000000000000000" renders "250 OP". The descriptor's value field has params threshold "0x8000…" and message "Unlimited", but no case uses a value at or above the threshold. ERC20._spendAllowance in GovernanceToken.sol treats type(uint256).max as an allowance that is never used up.
findings.fix: Add a test case with value = 2^256-1 and expect "Max spending amount: Unlimited".

findings.title: Permit intent "Authorize spending of tokens" names neither OP nor the spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json intent "Authorize spending of tokens". The fields show the token through tokenPath @.to ("250 OP") and show the spender. The intent line alone does not say which token or which party.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Allow {spender} to spend {value}".

Permit(address owner,address spender,uin.worst: Permit test only covers a finite amount; the "Unlimited" threshold message is never exercised.
